source.note: Written in a Claude Code session from the bible and pipeline prompt (no API key available); validated with src/dialogue/validate.ts.

greeting: Oh! Inspector. I'm sorry, I've never been questioned before. Not by a real one. Is {victim} really—? Oh dear.
I keep thinking about {victim}. I'll answer anything. I'll probably answer too much. I do that.
Please don't mind my hands, they always shake. It isn't guilt. It's just hands.
In novels this is where the detective is terribly kind to the nervous girl. I do hope you've read the same novels.
{Victim.full}, dead. I wrote a scene like this once, and it was nothing like this. Nothing at all.
Sorry — I was told to come. Should I sit? I'll sit. Sorry.
whereabouts: I was {room}, {time}. I think. Yes. I'm almost sure.
{RoomName}, {time}. I remember because the light was doing something interesting.
I was {room}. {Time}, that would have been. Is that helpful? I'd like to be helpful.
Let me think — {time} — yes, {room}. Sorry. Yes.
{Time} I was {room}, if that's what you need. It'll be in my notebook somewhere.
I'm fairly certain I was {room} {time}. Fairly. No — certain.
{RoomName}. {Time}. I'm sorry, is that a suspicious place to be? It didn't feel suspicious.
sawOne: {Other} was there. {Other.subject} barely looked up. People don't, mostly.
I saw {other}. I'm afraid I stared a bit. I stare at everyone; it's for the book.
Only {other}. We nodded. Well, I nodded. I'm not sure {other.subject} did.
There was {other}. I didn't say anything. I never know what to say.
sawSeveral: {Others}. Quite a little scene, really. I wanted to write it all down.
There were {others}. I stood near the wall. I'm good at walls.
Oh, {others}. Everyone talking and me not.
I saw {others}. I could tell you what each of them was wearing, if that helps? No? Sorry.
{Others} were there. I counted. I always count people; it's a nervous thing.
Let me see — {others}. Yes, I'm sure. I notice people more than they notice me.
sawVictim: {Victim} was there. Alive. I keep thinking that — alive.
I saw {victim}. {Victim.subject} smiled at me. Or near me. Oh, it's horrible.
{Victim} — yes. If I'd known, I'd have said something. Anything.
I saw {victim}. I've been trying to remember {victim.possessive} face exactly, and I can't, and I'm meant to be a writer.
Oh. {Victim}. Yes. That's the last time I— oh dear.
{Victim} was there, looking perfectly ordinary. That's what's so dreadful. Ordinary.
sawNoOne: No one. I'm sorry. I know that sounds bad.
Nobody, I'm afraid. I'm often in nobody's company.
I didn't see anyone. I was rather wrapped up in my own head. I usually am.
Not a soul. It was very quiet. I like quiet. Is that suspicious?
No one. Oh, that's no use to you at all, is it?
Nobody saw me and I saw nobody. That's — not good, is it?
confrontCrack: {Witness} said that? Oh no. Oh, I'm so sorry, I'll tell you everything—
Oh. Oh, {witness} said that. All right. All right. I lied. I'm terrible at it.
I knew someone would see. I knew it. Please don't be angry—
I can't— Yes. {Witness} is right. I'm sorry. Here's the truth.
confrontDeflect: {Witness} must be mistaken. I — I'm sure {witness.subject}'s mistaken.
No. No, I know what I said. I'm not changing it. Even if my voice is shaking.
I'm sorry, but {witness} is wrong. People mix me up with the furniture.
I've told you where I was. Please don't make me say it again; I'll only get it muddled.
accusedWrongly: Me? With {weapon}? I can't even open my own suitcase!
I didn't! I couldn't! I faint at paper cuts, Inspector!
Oh, this is exactly what happens in chapter nine, and it's always wrong in chapter nine.
Please — I liked {victim}. I like nearly everyone. I'm so frightened.
accusedRightly: I— yes. Yes. {Weapon}. I didn't mean— I did mean it. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.
You worked it out. Of course you did. I'd have written you exactly like that. {Victim} would have liked you.
{Victim.subject} read my notebook, Inspector. Every page. {Victim.subject} was going to tell everyone what I'd written.
It was {roomName}. It was so quick. I keep waiting to wake up.
opinion.marble: {Other} frightens me. {Other.subject} looks at you as though working out what you'd fetch.
I based a villain on {other} once. Then I worried that was unfair. Then I met {other.object} again.
{Other.subject} has very cold hands. I shook one. I'm not sure why I'm telling you that.
opinion.folder: {Other} is very correct. Everything about {other.object} is ironed.
{Other.subject} keeps asking why I want the passenger list. I can't exactly tell {other.object}.
I think {other} is lonely. A purser's office must be a lonely place.
opinion.mallet: {Other} is marvellous. {Other.subject} told me I need fresh air. {Other.subject}'s probably right.
I'd like to be more like {other}. Loud. Certain. Good at hitting things.
{Other.subject} once carried my deckchair without being asked. I nearly cried.
opinion.bear: {Other} tells me everything about everyone. I'm afraid I write it all down.
{Other.subject}'s very kind to me. Overwhelming, but kind. Like weather.
I don't think {other} has ever had a secret {other.subject} didn't share by teatime.
opinion.pail: {Other} brings me ginger biscuits for the seasickness. {Other.subject} doesn't have to. {Other.subject} just does.
Oh — {other}. {Other.subject}'s very— nice. To everyone. Not just me. Obviously.
{Other.subject} notices things. I think {other.subject} would make a good writer, actually.
eulogy.marble: {Other}? Dead? But {other.subject} was so — solid. I didn't think anything could happen to {other.object}.
I was frightened of {other.object}, and now I feel awful about it.
{Other.subject} never once said good morning to me. I don't know why that's the thing I keep thinking of.
eulogy.folder: Poor {other}. {Other.subject} was always so worried about doing things properly.
{Other.subject} told me off for being on the wrong deck once. Now I'd give anything to be told off.
Who'll keep the ledgers now? Sorry. That's a stupid thing to say. I say stupid things when I'm upset.
eulogy.mallet: Not {other}. {Other.subject} was the strongest person aboard. If it could happen to {other.object}—
{Other.subject} told me to stand up straight. I'm standing up straight now. For {other.object}.
{Other} was going to win the tournament. Everyone said so. {Other.subject} said so loudest.
eulogy.bear: {Other} called me little Edith. Nobody else ever called me anything.
The ship's so quiet without {other.object}. You don't realise how much someone talks until they stop.
{Other.subject} knew everyone's secrets. Do you think that's why? Oh, I hope that's not why.
eulogy.pail: {Other}? Oh no. Oh no. {Other.subject} brought me biscuits only yesterday.
{Other.subject} was kind to me when no one needed to be. I'm sorry, give me a moment.
{Other.subject} saw everything on this ship. I suppose someone didn't like being seen.
